title: TIROS-1, the first weather satellite
text: Sent back the first television pictures of Earth's clouds from orbit. It is still up there.

title: Yuri Gagarin orbits Earth
text: Vostok 1 carried the first human into space for a single 108-minute orbit.

title: Telstar 1
text: Relayed the first live transatlantic television. Long dead, it still circles Earth.

title: Alouette 1, Canada's first satellite
text: Studied the ionosphere for ten years, and is still in orbit today.

title: Valentina Tereshkova
text: Vostok 6 made her the first woman in space, for almost three days and 48 orbits.

title: Syncom 2, the first geosynchronous satellite
text: It circled Earth once a day, tracing a figure-eight over the Atlantic.

title: Syncom 3, the first geostationary satellite
text: Hung over the Pacific and broadcast the Tokyo Olympics to the United States.

title: The first spacewalk
text: Alexei Leonov left Voskhod 2 for twelve minutes, and struggled to get back in.

title: Early Bird (Intelsat I)
text: The first commercial communications satellite, in geostationary orbit.

title: Astérix, France's first satellite
text: France became the third country to launch a satellite on its own rocket.

title: Gemini 8: the first docking
text: Neil Armstrong and David Scott docked with an Agena target, then had to undock from a spinning stack.

title: Apollo 11 lifts off
text: Four days later, Armstrong and Aldrin walked on the Moon.

title: Ohsumi, Japan's first satellite
text: Japan became the fourth country to put a satellite into orbit.

title: Dong Fang Hong 1, China's first satellite
text: It played the song 'The East Is Red' from orbit. It has never come down.

title: Salyut 1, the first space station
text: The Soviet station hosted one crew for 23 days in 1971.

title: Prospero, the UK's only satellite on its own rocket
text: Launched on Black Arrow from Woomera, Australia; it is still in orbit.

title: Landsat 1
text: The start of the longest continuous record of Earth's land surface from space.

title: Skylab
text: America's first space station; three crews lived aboard before it fell over Australia in 1979.

title: Apollo–Soyuz
text: American and Soviet spacecraft docked in orbit two days later: a handshake in space.

title: Salyut 6
text: The first station with two docking ports, so supply ships could visit crews.

title: Navstar 1, the first GPS satellite
text: The first of the constellation that now guides almost every phone on Earth.

title: The first Space Shuttle flight
text: Columbia flew STS-1, twenty years to the day after Gagarin.

title: Salyut 7
text: Famously revived by a crew in 1985 after it lost power and froze.

title: The first untethered spacewalk
text: Bruce McCandless flew free of Challenger on the Manned Maneuvering Unit.

title: Challenger
text: The Shuttle broke apart 73 seconds after launch, killing its crew of seven.

title: Mir's core module
text: The first modular space station, crewed almost continuously for ten years.

title: The first Hubble servicing mission
text: Endeavour's crew fitted corrective optics that fixed Hubble's blurred vision.

title: Shuttle docks with Mir
text: Atlantis and Mir formed the largest spacecraft yet, a rehearsal for the ISS.

title: The first Iridium satellites
text: The start of the first satellite phone constellation, and of its famous flares.

title: John Glenn returns to space
text: At 77, the first American to orbit Earth flew again on Discovery.

title: Unity joins Zarya
text: The first US module of the ISS, connected to Zarya in orbit days later.

title: Chandra X-ray Observatory
text: Still working, on a long elliptical orbit reaching a third of the way to the Moon.

title: Terra
text: NASA's flagship Earth-observing satellite, imaging the whole planet every one to two days.

title: Expedition 1 launches
text: The crew that began over two decades of continuous human presence on the ISS.

title: People move into the ISS
text: Someone has been living in orbit every day since.

title: Mir comes down
text: After 15 years, the station was steered into the South Pacific.

title: Aqua
text: Measures Earth's water cycle: clouds, rain, sea ice and snow.

title: Columbia
text: The Shuttle broke up on re-entry over Texas, killing its crew of seven.

title: Yang Liwei, China's first astronaut
text: Shenzhou 5 made China the third country to fly people into orbit on its own.

title: USA-193 shot down
text: A US Navy missile destroyed a failed spy satellite low enough that its debris soon fell back.

title: Falcon 1 reaches orbit
text: SpaceX's fourth try made it the first privately developed liquid-fuelled rocket to reach orbit.

title: The last Hubble servicing mission
text: Atlantis's crew left Hubble better than ever, with no more visits planned.

title: The last Space Shuttle launch
text: Atlantis flew STS-135 to the ISS, ending thirty years of Shuttle flights.

title: Dragon, the first commercial ship to the ISS
text: SpaceX's capsule was berthed to the station three days later.

title: A rocket lands itself
text: A Falcon 9 first stage came back to Cape Canaveral after putting 11 satellites in orbit.

title: India's anti-satellite test
text: Mission Shakti destroyed a satellite at about 280 km; most of the debris fell within months.

title: Crew Dragon's first crew
text: The first astronauts launched from the US since 2011, and the first on a commercial spacecraft.
